name: Franklin's kite and the rod that actually worked
scope: Lightning is electricity -- and the dangerous test was not the famous one. T1: June 1752, a Philadelphia thunderstorm -- Benjamin Franklin and his son William fly a silk kite; loose fibres on the wet hemp string stand up and push each other apart, and Franklin draws a spark from a brass key into a Leyden jar (the hook: the KEY sparked). T2: CORRECTED MISCONCEPTION -- the kite was NOT struck by lightning; a direct strike would almost certainly have killed him. The storm cloud overhead INDUCED charge on the wet string, and he sheltered in a shed keeping a dry silk cord between his hand and the key. T3: Franklin was not first to run his own idea -- he had PUBLISHED the design (an insulated 'sentry box' with a pointed iron rod) in 1749-50, and Thomas-Francois Dalibard built it at Marly-la-Ville outside Paris on 10 May 1752 with a 40-foot iron rod and drew sparks a month before the kite. The proposal travelled faster than the proposer. T4: the genuinely lethal rung -- Georg Wilhelm Richmann, repeating it in St Petersburg in 1753 with an UNGROUNDED conductor, was killed instantly when a discharge struck his forehead, leaving a red mark and singed hair. T4b: the applied test that actually worked -- a pointed rod bonded to a thick conductor running all the way to damp earth, giving the strike a path that isn't the building. T5: the tip-shape war -- Franklin's pointed rods vs Benjamin Wilson's blunt ones, argued at the Purfleet powder magazine and turned political during the American Revolution, with George III fitting knobs to his palace. T5b: honest caveat -- historian Tom Tucker (Bolt of Fate, 2003) argues Franklin may never have flown the kite at all; Franklin's own 1752 Pennsylvania Gazette notice was brief, and the vivid version comes from Joseph Priestley's 1767 history written fifteen years later. The ROD is the part that is unquestionably his and unquestionably worked.
source: Grokipedia: /page/Kite_experiment, /page/Lightning_rod, /page/Benjamin_Franklin, /page/1753 (Richmann), /page/Atmospheric_electricity; Wikipedia: Kite_experiment (Franklin not struck; Tucker 2003 skepticism; Oct 1752 Pennsylvania Gazette; Priestley 1767)
framing_note: DISCOVERY + a corrected-misconception spine. The dinner-test payoff is T2: he was not struck, and if he had been he would have died -- the picture-book image is wrong. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: never let a rung say or imply lightning hit the kite; and every rung must carry the danger honestly (Richmann died doing this) -- the bank NEVER frames this as a try-it-at-home. The one safe invitation in this territory is counting seconds between flash and thunder (belongs to the static-electricity ladder). Distractor mine = the live wrong theories of 1750: the abbe Nollet's two-fluid effluvia-and-affluences, lightning as a sulphurous exhalation, ringing church bells to break up storms, and real rival experimenters (Dalibard, de Romas, Richmann, Wilson). Anti-restatement: never say 'lightning is electrical' in a stem that then asks what the kite showed -- describe the fibres standing apart and the key and let the conclusion be recalled. LANE: history owns Franklin the Founder and the diplomacy; science keys the EXPERIMENT, the induced charge, and the rod.
history_overlap: history bank: Benjamin Franklin as Founding Father / Revolutionary diplomat (and possibly the Turgot epigram) -- science must key only the sentry-box/kite/rod experiment and Richmann's death, not Franklin's politics.

name: The twitching frog: Galvani versus Volta
scope: A dispute so stubborn that settling it produced the battery. T1: Bologna in the 1780s -- Luigi Galvani's dissected frog legs, hanging from a brass hook against an iron railing, KICK as if alive with no storm and no electrical machine anywhere. T2: Galvani's claim -- 'animal electricity', a fluid stored in the animal itself with the nerve as its conductor; he believed he had found the force of life. T3: Alessandro Volta's counter-claim and the test -- the twitch came from the two DIFFERENT metals joined through a moist conductor, not from the frog; the frog was merely the most sensitive detector anyone had (Volta got the same effect on his own tongue with two metals, no frog required). T4: to end the argument Volta BUILT the alternative -- a stack of zinc and copper discs separated by brine-soaked cardboard, announced to Sir Joseph Banks of the Royal Society on 20 March 1800 as an 'artificial electric organ'. The first battery was a rebuttal. T4b: what the new tool did within months -- in May 1800 William Nicholson and Anthony Carlisle used a pile to split water into hydrogen and oxygen; on 6 October 1807 Humphry Davy, running hundreds of cells, pulled metallic potassium out of molten potash, a metal nobody had ever seen. T5: the honest verdict -- BOTH men were right about different things. Volta explained the frog-leg experiment; Galvani was right that animals really do generate electricity, as his own contraction-without-metals work suggested and as Emil du Bois-Reymond proved in the 1840s with sensitive galvanometers measuring real nerve currents. Your nerves are firing electrically as you read the question. T5b: the spectacle -- 18 January 1803, Galvani's nephew Giovanni Aldini applies a voltaic battery to the corpse of hanged murderer George Forster at the Royal College of Surgeons in London; the jaw quivers, an eye opens, a fist clenches.
framing_note: REVERSAL/DISPUTE ladder whose soul is that a scientific argument was settled by BUILDING something. Dinner-test payoff: T5b (the corpse's eye opening) for the shiver; the intellectual payoff is T5 (both men were right about different things) and that rung must be the ladder's closing note. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: do NOT teach 'Volta disproved animal electricity' -- bioelectricity is real and now textbook; Volta refuted Galvani's EXPLANATION OF THE FROG-LEG EFFECT, not the existence of animal electricity. Second rail: Mary Shelley's 1818 Frankenstein never states how the creature was animated; galvanism appears in her 1831 introduction and in the 1816 Villa Diodati conversations -- say it that way, do not claim the novel describes it. Distractor mine = live wrong theories of exactly that decade: vitalism / the vital fluid, Mesmer's animal magnetism, Nollet's effluvia, phlogiston -- plus real rivals (Aldini, Scarpa, Banks, Nicholson). Anti-restatement: never let a stem mention 'two different metals' before asking what Volta claimed. LANE: the electric eel's organ and electroreception are ANIMAL-bank adaptations; science owns the Galvani-Volta discovery and bioelectricity's mechanism.
history_overlap: animal bank: electric eels / electroreception as creature adaptations -- science must not build a rung on the eel's biology, only on Galvani's frog as an INSTRUMENT and on human nerve currents.

name: Oersted's needle -- and the accident that wasn't
scope: One twitching compass merged two forces. T1: Copenhagen, April 1820 -- Hans Christian Oersted switches on a current in a wire lying near a compass during a demonstration for advanced students, and the needle swings off north. T2: the counter-intuitive detail -- the needle does not point AT the wire or lie along it; it settles at RIGHT ANGLES to it, and flips the other way when he reverses the battery leads. That right-angle twist is the fingerprint of a magnetic field that CIRCLES the wire rather than pointing at it. T3: CORRECTED MISCONCEPTION (the gold rung) -- the beloved story that this was a lucky accident during a lecture is a myth. Oersted had been hunting an electricity-magnetism link since 1818 because he was a Kantian who believed the forces of nature were fundamentally one; the demonstration was the moment the hunt paid off, and he then spent about three months on systematic tests before publishing. T3b: how he published -- a four-page Latin pamphlet, 'Experimenta circa effectum conflictus electrici in acum magneticam', dated 21 July 1820, posted privately to scientists across Europe rather than submitted to a journal. T4: the speed of the response -- Arago reported it to the French Academy on 4 September 1820, and within DAYS Andre-Marie Ampere showed that two parallel current-carrying wires attract when the currents run the same way and repel when they oppose: no magnet needed at all, current alone does it. By late September he had presented the work and named the new science electrodynamics. T5: what it broke -- since Gilbert in 1600, electricity and magnetism had been filed as separate forces (Gilbert had explicitly separated them), and Coulomb had argued they could not interconvert. One deflected needle merged them. T5b: kid test -- lay a compass under a short wire from a single AA cell (with a resistor, briefly) and watch the needle move; reverse the leads and watch it reverse.
source: Grokipedia: /page/Hans_Christian_%C3%98rsted, /page/Electromagnetism, /page/History_of_electromagnetic_theory, /page/Andr%C3%A9-Marie_Amp%C3%A8re, /page/Amp%C3%A8re's_force_law; Wikipedia: Hans_Christian_Orsted (explicitly: 'the often reported story that Orsted made this discovery incidentally during a lecture is a myth'; searching since 1818; Kantian unity of nature)
framing_note: DISCOVERY ladder built around a myth-correction, which makes it doubly on-voice. Dinner-test payoff: T3 -- the textbook 'happy accident' is false, and the truer story (a man who went looking for years because of a philosophical conviction) is better. NOTE THE SEED WAS WRONG HERE: do not build any rung on 'lecture-table accident' as fact; if the accident version appears at all it must appear as the myth being corrected. Second accuracy rail: the deflection is PERPENDICULAR to the wire -- never write it as the needle pointing toward the wire. Distractor mine = the respectable wrong positions of 1820: that electricity and magnetism were separate imponderable fluids, Coulomb's explicit non-interconversion claim, the electric 'atmosphere', plus real adjacent people (Ampere, Arago, Biot, Savart, Schweigger). Anti-restatement: never say 'a current makes a magnetic field' in a stem that then asks what Oersted saw. Intra-bank note: Ampere's force law gets ONE rung here -- do not let this ladder become an Ampere ladder.

name: Faraday, the bookbinder's apprentice
scope: The greatest experimentalist of the century had almost no schooling and almost no mathematics. T1: a fourteen-year-old London bookbinder's apprentice read the books passing through his hands -- including Jane Marcet's Conversations on Chemistry -- and taught himself science off the workbench. T2: at twenty he attended Humphry Davy's Royal Institution lectures, wrote up 300 pages of notes, BOUND them himself into a book, sent it to Davy asking for work -- and was hired as chemical assistant on 1 March 1813. T2b: 1821 -- he makes a current-carrying wire circle endlessly around a magnet standing in a dish of mercury: the first device ever to turn electricity into continuous motion. T3: the ugly part -- he published it without properly crediting William Hyde Wollaston's earlier suggestion, and the row soured his relationship with Davy, his own mentor. T3b: 29 August 1831, the ring -- two separate coils wound on opposite sides of a soft iron ring, one to a battery of ten plates, the other to a galvanometer. The needle kicks at the INSTANT the battery is connected, kicks the other way when it is broken, and does nothing at all while the current sits steady. T4: that 'only at the instant' IS the law -- a steady magnetic field induces nothing; only a CHANGING one drives current. Weeks later that autumn he thrust a bar magnet in and out of a coil by hand, getting current from muscle power alone, then spun a copper disc between magnet poles for the first generator. T4b: 1836 -- he builds a twelve-foot cube of wood and wire mesh, climbs inside with an electroscope, has the outside charged, and nothing inside stirs; charge lives on the OUTSIDE of a conductor (test it: a radio wrapped in foil goes silent). T5: he had no calculus -- his tool was the 'lines of force' he drew -- and Maxwell nevertheless read him as a mathematician of a very high order and turned those lines into equations; the FIELD, the idea that space itself carries the action, is Faraday's. T5b: CORRECTED MISCONCEPTION -- the famous retort to a politician ('Of what use is a new-born baby?', or 'you will soon be able to tax it') appears nowhere in Faraday's writings or his contemporaries', surfaced only after his death, and Gladstone, the usual attributee, did not become Prime Minister until the year AFTER Faraday died. T5c: he refused a knighthood and twice refused the presidency of the Royal Society, preferring to stay plain Mr Faraday; buried at Highgate with a memorial near Newton in Westminster Abbey; founder of the Christmas Lectures for children that still run.
source: Grokipedia: /page/Michael_Faraday, /page/Faraday's_law_of_induction, /page/Faraday_cage, /page/Electromagnetic_induction, /page/Dynamo; Wikipedia: Michael_Faraday (Marcet; 300-page bound notes; hired 1 March 1813; Wollaston controversy; 1836 12-ft cage; 1843 ice-pail; refused knighthood and RS presidency twice; Highgate burial + Westminster plaque; 19 Christmas Lectures 1827-60), Faraday's_law_of_induction (29 Aug 1831 ring; changing field required; Henry published later); Snopes fact-check 'Michael Faraday Tax Quote' (apocryphal; Gladstone PM only after Faraday's death)
framing_note: KEYSTONE DISCOVERY ladder. Two payoffs: the dinner-test rung is T2 (a poor apprentice bound his own lecture notes into a book and that got him the job); the on-voice skepticism rung is T5b (the beloved quote nobody can source -- test even the stories you love). HARD ACCURACY RAIL: Joseph Henry independently observed induction but published later -- never write a rung implying Faraday was the only person who saw it; and the exact October 1831 dates for the moving-magnet and disc experiments should be checked against Faraday's Diary before use, otherwise say 'weeks later that autumn'. Second rail: Faraday's mathematics was limited to simple algebra -- that is the wonder, do not soften it or exaggerate it into 'no education at all' (he read voraciously and lectured for decades). Distractor mine = real rivals and mentors (Wollaston, Davy, Henry, Ampere, Oersted) and the wrong expectation that made induction take ten years to find -- that a magnet sitting near a coil should push a steady current. Anti-restatement: describe the galvanometer kicking only at make and break, and let 'a changing field' be recalled knowledge, not read off the stem. Intra-bank: Davy's chemistry (potassium, the safety lamp) belongs to the chemistry sub-strand -- keep Davy here as mentor and gatekeeper only.

name: Maxwell: the number that turned out to be light
scope: A calculation about coils and jars produced the speed of light. T1: working from Faraday's picture of lines of force, James Clerk Maxwell worked out how fast a ripple in a combined electric-and-magnetic field would travel -- and got about 310,000 km/s, within a hair of the measured speed of light. T2: the astonishing part -- the numbers he fed in had NOTHING to do with light. They came from laboratory measurements of electric and magnetic force (the 1856 Weber-Kohlrausch ratio), from charged jars and current-carrying coils in a German laboratory. He wrote in On Physical Lines of Force (1861-62) that 'we can scarcely avoid the inference that light consists in the transverse undulations of the same medium which is the cause of electric and magnetic phenomena'. T3: the piece he had to invent -- current flowing into a capacitor stops dead at the gap, yet the magnetic field around it does not stop; Maxwell added the 'displacement current', a CHANGING ELECTRIC FIELD acting like a current, to close the circuit. Delete that one term and electromagnetic waves do not exist. T3b: the mechanism a paragraph can carry -- a changing electric field makes a magnetic field whose change makes an electric field, the two regenerating each other outward across empty space. That is why sunlight crosses the vacuum with nothing to wave in. T4: CORRECTED MISCONCEPTION -- Maxwell never wrote 'the four equations'. His 1865 A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field had twenty equations in twenty variables; Oliver Heaviside, a self-taught former telegraph operator, compressed them into the four vector equations everyone now calls Maxwell's, in the mid-1880s. T4b: one consequence -- visible light, radio, infrared and X-rays are the SAME phenomenon at different wavelengths, one spectrum with one mechanism. T5: it was a PREDICTION, and it sat untested for over twenty years until Hertz made the waves in a room. T5b: the honest caveat -- Maxwell believed the waves rippled through a luminiferous ether, and there is no ether; the equations survived the picture that produced them.
source: Grokipedia: /page/James_Clerk_Maxwell, /page/Maxwell%27s_equations, /page/History_of_Maxwell's_equations, /page/Displacement_current, /page/A_Dynamical_Theory_of_the_Electromagnetic_Field; Wikipedia: On_Physical_Lines_of_Force; MacTutor (St Andrews) 'The Electromagnetic Field -- James Clerk Maxwell' for the 1862 'we can scarcely avoid the inference...' passage and the Fizeau comparison
framing_note: UNIFICATION ladder; the analytic ceiling of this sub-strand but still a paragraph-level mechanism, no vector calculus, no PDEs -- describe the regenerating fields in words, never write the equations. Dinner-test payoff: T2 -- the speed of light fell out of measurements made with jars and coils, by people who were not studying light. Second gold rung: T4 (Heaviside, not Maxwell, gave us 'the four equations'). HARD ACCURACY RAIL: Maxwell's medium was the ether and he meant it literally -- tell it as right equations inside a picture that was later abandoned, never retrofit him with modern field-in-vacuum language. Use the 1862 quotation verbatim or not at all. Distractor mine = the graveyard: the luminiferous ether, action-at-a-distance, corpuscular light, caloric -- plus real adjacent people (Faraday, Weber, Kohlrausch, Fizeau, Heaviside, Hertz). Anti-restatement: never let a stem say the two constants were electrical before asking where his number came from. Intra-bank: the 'one speed of light for every observer' puzzle is the RELATIVITY ladder's -- at most a single closing pointer here, never a rung that teaches relativity.
history_overlap: philosophy bank: prediction-then-confirmation as an epistemology move (Popper-style) -- science must key the WORKING PRACTICE (a number predicted before it was measured) and leave the seminar framing to philosophy.

name: Hertz makes the waves and calls them useless
scope: The man who proved Maxwell right could not see what he had. T1: Karlsruhe, 1886-88, a darkened laboratory -- Hertz cranks a spark across two brass spheres, and a plain loop of wire standing metres away, connected to nothing, sparks in sympathy across a gap so small he has to squint to see it. T2: to prove it was a WAVE and not just a jolt, he bounced it off a zinc sheet so outgoing and reflected waves interfered, then walked his detector along the room finding live spots and dead spots; their spacing gave a wavelength of about four metres, and wavelength times frequency gave the speed of light. T3: he then did to invisible radio everything a schoolbook does to light -- reflected it off metal mirrors, refracted it through a prism of pitch, polarised it with a grid of parallel wires. Same behaviour, same speed, different wavelength: Maxwell confirmed with hardware. T3b: the blindness -- asked what use it was, Hertz is REPORTED to have answered that it was of no use whatsoever, just an experiment proving Maestro Maxwell right. He died at 36 on 1 January 1894; reading Augusto Righi's memorial article on Hertz's work, a 21-year-old Guglielmo Marconi began attic experiments near Bologna in 1895 and built the thing Hertz saw no use for. T4: the SECOND blindness in the same apparatus -- in 1887 Hertz noticed his receiver sparked more readily when ultraviolet light fell on the gap. He wrote it up in Annalen der Physik and moved on. That side note was the photoelectric effect, the anomaly Einstein explained with light quanta in 1905 and the work he was actually awarded the Nobel for. T5: the lesson the bank keeps -- the waves existed on paper before they existed in a room, and the person who first made them real was the worst-placed person alive to judge what they were for.
source: Grokipedia: /page/Heinrich_Hertz, /page/Spark-gap_transmitter, /page/Photoelectric_effect, /page/Invention_of_radio; Wikipedia: Heinrich_Hertz (dipole with 7.5 mm gap fed by a Ruhmkorff coil, ~50 MHz; zinc reflector ~12 m, ~4 m waves; reflection/refraction/polarisation 1886-89; 1887 UV observation in Annalen der Physik; died 1 Jan 1894 aged 36; the 'of no use whatsoever' quote sourced only to a secondary reference); marconiheritage.org and Righi-Marconi literature for Righi's 1894 memorial article prompting Marconi's 1895 work
framing_note: DISCOVERY ladder whose point is a discoverer's blindness -- told without mockery; Hertz's stated purpose (testing Maxwell) was a perfectly good purpose. Dinner-test payoff: T4 -- he found the photoelectric effect, wrote it down, and shrugged. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: the 'of no use whatsoever' line is REPORTED, traced only to secondary sources, not to a Hertz manuscript -- if the bank uses it, the stem must say 'reportedly told his students', and the safer factual rung is that he undertook the work to test Maxwell and saw no application. Do not claim Marconi met or corresponded with Hertz -- the link is Righi's memorial article. Distractor mine = real rivals and adjacent apparatus (Oliver Lodge, Branly's coherer, Jagadish Chandra Bose, Tesla, Righi) and the wrong contemporary expectation that the waves needed a wire or moved through the ether at some other speed. Anti-restatement: never let a stem mention ultraviolet light before asking what Hertz noticed at the spark gap. LANE: Marconi's wireless as a world-changing business (and the Titanic) is HISTORY -- science gets one pointer rung, keyed to the irony, not the shipping story.
history_overlap: history bank: Marconi, transatlantic wireless and the Titanic distress calls as a turn-of-the-century episode -- science keys only Hertz's test of Maxwell and the Righi-article link, not the wireless industry.

name: The war of the currents, told honestly
scope: A commercial fight decided by a piece of physics. T1: 4 September 1882, Edison's Pearl Street Station lights lower Manhattan on DIRECT current -- and the system has a hard geographical limit: at usable household voltage DC fades out after roughly a mile, so a city needs a power station every mile. T2: THE MECHANISM RUNG -- a transformer works only on ALTERNATING current. Step the voltage up and the current carrying the same power falls; heating loss in the wire goes as current SQUARED, so high-voltage AC crosses a hundred miles on modest copper and is stepped back down at the far end. That equation, not a personality, is why the wire on your street is AC. T3: the missing piece was a motor that would run on it -- Nikola Tesla's answer, patented in 1888, feeds out-of-step currents into separate coils so the magnetic field itself ROTATES and drags the rotor around, with no brushes and no sparking; Westinghouse licensed the patents that year. T3b: Edison's counter-campaign, told straight -- his associates staged public electrocutions of animals using Westinghouse AC machines, and Harold Brown pushed New York to specify AC for its new electric chair; William Kemmler's botched execution on 6 August 1890 produced exactly the association that side wanted. T4: how it actually ended -- not with a duel but with a bid. Westinghouse underbid Edison's people to light the 1893 Chicago World's Columbian Exposition, running about 100,000 lamps in front of millions of visitors, then built the Niagara Falls generators that carried power over twenty miles to Buffalo. T4b: CORRECTED MISCONCEPTION -- Topsy the elephant, killed at Coney Island on 4 January 1903 and filmed by a company bearing Edison's name, is endlessly retold as Edison's anti-AC stunt. The current war was years over, Edison no longer ran the company that carried his name, and no document ties him to it. T5: the honest ledger -- Edison was not a cartoon villain (low-voltage DC genuinely is safer in a house, and DC came back for long-distance HVDC links and runs every battery-powered thing you own); Tesla was a real genius whose later claims outran his evidence; and George Westinghouse, the least-remembered of the three, is the one who actually built the grid.
source: Grokipedia: /page/War_of_the_currents, /page/Nikola_Tesla, /page/Rotating_magnetic_field, /page/Polyphase_system, /page/Induction_motor, /page/William_Kemmler, /page/Westinghouse_Electric_Company; Rutgers Thomas Edison Papers 'Myth Buster -- Topsy the Elephant'; Smithsonian Magazine 'Topsy the Elephant Was a Victim of Her Captors, Not Thomas Edison'
framing_note: DISCOVERY/RIVALRY ladder with a hard even-handedness requirement -- the seed brief says no cartoon villain and the bank's rails say the documented record is damning enough. Dinner-test payoff: T4b (the Topsy story everyone repeats is false). The ANALYTIC anchor is T2: this must be the physics rung, or the ladder degenerates into gossip. HARD ACCURACY RAILS, two: (1) Topsy -- Edison had no documented involvement and the current war was already over; (2) Tesla's celebrated story of Edison's promised $50,000 bonus and the 'you don't understand our American humour' line comes ONLY from Tesla's much later autobiography and is uncorroborated -- do not seed a rung on it as fact. Verify the exact Niagara-to-Buffalo distance and the 1895 generation vs 1896 transmission dates before writing a numeric rung. Distractor mine = real rival technologies and people: Gaulard and Gibbs transformers, William Stanley's 1886 Great Barrington demonstration, Elihu Thomson, Charles Brush arc lighting, Ferranti in London. LANE: history owns the Gilded Age and the 1893 fair as an American episode; science keys the I-squared-R transmission argument and the rotating field.
history_overlap: history bank: the Gilded Age industrialists and the 1893 Chicago World's Columbian Exposition as a history episode -- science must key the transmission physics and the induction motor, and use the fair only as the settlement of a technical bet.

name: A nail, a wire and a battery: the electromagnet
scope: The most kid-buildable machine in physics, and the switch it became. T1: 1825 -- William Sturgeon varnishes a horseshoe of soft iron, winds eighteen turns of BARE copper wire round it, connects a single cell, and the seven-ounce lump lifts nine pounds of iron, over twenty times its own weight. Break the circuit and the load drops instantly. T2: why the iron matters -- the bare wire's own field is feeble; the iron core's internal magnetic domains swing into line with it and add their own, multiplying the field enormously, then letting go the moment the current stops. T3: Joseph Henry's improvement was insulation. Sturgeon's bare wire could only be laid in one loose layer or the current would short across the turns; Henry wrapped his wire in silk thread, packed hundreds of tight turns in stacked layers, and built magnets that lifted over 2,000 pounds -- because the field follows turns TIMES current, not wire thickness. T3b: what Henry did with it -- at the Albany Academy in 1831 he strung about a mile of wire round a room and made a distant electromagnet strike a bell; that is the telegraph's working principle, and Samuel Morse built a business on Henry's relay. T4: the deep idea is the RELAY -- a small current works an electromagnet that closes a switch carrying a big one, so a weak signal controls a strong one. That is the ancestor of every switching element in a computer. T4b: Henry independently observed induction before Faraday published and discovered self-inductance, the sharp 'kick' a coil delivers when you break its circuit; the unit of inductance carries his name, and Faraday's priority rests on publishing first. T5: KID TEST -- a steel nail, a metre or two of insulated wire and one AA cell make a magnet that picks up paperclips; count the clips, add ten turns, count again, and you have measured turns-times-current yourself.
framing_note: MECHANISM ladder with an explicit build-it invitation -- the test-it-yourself soul of the sub-strand. The hook rung is T1 (twenty times its own weight); the payoff rung is T5, the invitation. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: keep the numbers honest -- Sturgeon's magnet weighed about seven ounces and lifted nine pounds with one cell; Henry's largest lifted over 2,000 pounds; do not inflate either, and do not say the electricity 'magnetises the iron permanently' (soft iron releases when the current stops -- that release is the whole point of a relay). Safety note in context, not in stem: a shorted cell heats up, keep the test brief. Distractor mine = real alternatives and adjacent claims: lodestone and permanent steel magnets, Ampere's solenoid, Arago's rotating-disc effect, and the wrong belief that lifting power comes from the metal's own quality rather than turns times current. Anti-restatement: never mention silk insulation in a stem that then asks what Henry changed. LANE: the telegraph's transformation of the 19th century (Morse, the transatlantic cable) belongs to HISTORY -- science keys the relay MECHANISM and the silk-wrapped wire.
history_overlap: history bank: Morse, the telegraph and the transatlantic cable as a communications revolution -- science must key the electromagnet/relay mechanism and Henry's insulated winding, not the telegraph's social impact.

name: Static electricity: one phenomenon at three scales
scope: THEME ladder -- the balloon, the doorknob and the thunderbolt are the same thing, and the biggest one is unsolved. T1: a balloon rubbed on hair lifts scraps of paper and makes hair stand out; the Greeks got the same effect rubbing amber, whose Greek name elektron is the root of the word electricity. T2: 1745-46, bottling it -- Ewald von Kleist puts a brass wire through the cork of a medicine bottle on 11 October 1745 and is knocked back by the shock; Pieter van Musschenbroek at Leiden repeats it with a water-filled jar and writes that he would not take a second shock for the whole kingdom of France. Charge could now be stored. T3: 1746, the daftest great experiment -- Jean-Antoine Nollet links about two hundred Carthusian monks into a circle nearly a mile around with iron wire and discharges a Leyden jar through them; every monk jumps at once, showing the effect travels far too fast to time by eye. T3b: the mechanism -- rubbing does not CREATE charge, it MOVES it; one surface ends with a surplus of electrons and the other with a deficit, always equal and opposite, which you can check by holding both objects near a thin stream of water from a tap. T4: the doorknob scaled up -- air breaks down at roughly three million volts per metre, so a spark you can see jump one millimetre means thousands of volts; yet the total charge is minuscule, which is exactly why it stings and cannot hurt you, while lightning at the same volts-per-metre carries an enormous charge. T4b: how a thundercloud charges -- colliding ice crystals and graupel in the updraft strip charge from each other, light ice riding up positive and heavy graupel falling negative, until the cloud is a stacked battery kilometres tall. Kid test: count seconds between flash and thunder, about five per mile or three per kilometre. T4c: a naming choice you still live with -- Franklin's one-fluid model made him call one state positive and the other negative, so conventional current is drawn flowing from plus to minus in every circuit diagram, while the electrons actually drift the other way. T5: MYSTERY RUNG -- nobody knows how lightning STARTS. The strongest electric fields ever measured inside thunderclouds are roughly ten times too weak to break air down the way a laboratory spark does; cosmic-ray-triggered runaway electrons and ice-surface effects are candidates and the question is genuinely open. T5b: a second open one at the everyday end -- after 2,500 years, physicists still argue whether rubbing two insulators transfers electrons, ions, or scraps of material, and even nominally identical materials charge each other. The balloon on your head is not a solved problem.

framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder -- the spine is one mechanism (charge separation and breakdown) displayed across three scales, every rung a concrete named case. Payoff: T5, the MYSTERY rung -- the bank says 'no one yet knows' proudly, and no distractor on that rung may secretly be the truth. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: do NOT teach 'lightning is just static discharging to earth' as a complete explanation, and do not teach that clouds rub together -- the charging is ice-graupel collisional and the INITIATION is unsolved. Second rail: rubbing moves charge, never creates it. Distractor mine = the retired theories, used honestly: Nollet's two-fluid effluvia-and-affluences (he was a serious man and Franklin's real opponent), Franklin's one-fluid surplus/deficit (nearly right, and the source of the backwards current convention), the electric 'atmosphere', and the folk claim that clouds rub. Anti-restatement: on the Nollet rung describe the ring of monks and let the CONCLUSION (it propagates too fast to time) be recalled. LANE: geography owns lightning PLACES (Catatumbo, lightning capitals); science owns the charging mechanism and the open initiation problem.
history_overlap: geography bank: lightning-record places such as Lake Maracaibo / Catatumbo and thunderstorm geography -- science must key the charging mechanism, the volts-per-metre scaling and the unsolved initiation, never the place tour.

name: Ohm and the book called a web of naked fancies
scope: The law on every resistor was dismissed as fantasy, and the instrument is why it exists. T1: a Cologne schoolteacher with no laboratory budget builds his own apparatus and draws his own wire to measure something nobody had pinned down -- how much current a given electrical push drives through a given wire. T2: THE INSTRUMENT RUNG (the ladder's soul) -- his early attempts failed because a voltaic pile's output sags as it runs. Ohm swapped it for a copper-bismuth thermocouple with one junction in boiling water and the other in melting ice: a source that held steady all day. The stable source is what made the law findable at all. T3: what he found, published in 1827 as Die galvanische Kette, mathematisch bearbeitet -- current is proportional to the push and inversely proportional to the resistance, so doubling the length of the wire halves the current; he got there by treating electricity the way Fourier had treated heat flowing along a bar. T4: the reception -- German physicists called his mathematical treatment unphysical, 'a web of naked fancies'; his own school did not value it; he resigned his post and spent years in obscurity. T5: the vindication -- the Royal Society awarded him the Copley Medal in 1841, foreign membership followed, and in 1852 he finally got a professorship at Munich, two years before he died; the coloured stripes on every resistor in every device in the house are read in the unit that carries his name. T5b: the honest caveat -- 'Ohm's law' is not a law of nature like gravitation. It describes metals at steady temperature well and fails for a lamp filament as it heats, for a diode, for gas in a tube. Knowing where it breaks is knowing more than the law.
source: Grokipedia: /page/Georg_Ohm ('unphysical', 'a web of naked fancies'; Copley Medal 1841; copper-bismuth thermocouple with boiling-water and melting-ice junctions; voltaic-pile polarisation drove the 1826 switch), /page/Ohm%27s_law, /page/Thermocouple, /page/Thomas_Johann_Seebeck; Wikipedia: Georg_Ohm (1827 title; cold reception; resignation; Copley 1841; Munich 1852)
framing_note: REVERSAL ladder whose real teaching is METHOD: the measurement was impossible until the source stopped drifting. Dinner-test payoff: T4, the phrase 'a web of naked fancies' aimed at a book now printed on the side of every resistor. The method payoff is T2 and it must not be cut. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: 'a web of naked fancies' is the standard rendering of the hostile German reception -- attribute it to critics of the reception generally, NOT to a named Minister of Education, unless a primary source is found; the widely repeated ministerial attribution is shaky. Second rail: state plainly that Ohm's relation is an empirical description with known failures -- do not let a rung call it a universal law. Distractor mine = real adjacent laws and people: Fourier's heat conduction (his actual model), Coulomb, Ampere, Volta, Seebeck, Poggendorff's galvanometer -- plus the genuine pre-Ohm belief that a longer wire simply 'used up' more of the electric fluid. Anti-restatement: never mention a drifting battery in a stem that then asks what Ohm substituted for it. Voice: no rote symbol or formula recall -- the equation may be described in words, never asked as a bare definition.

name: The terrella: a model Earth on the bench
scope: THEME ladder -- twice in history, someone built a little Earth and learned something about the real one. T1: 1600 -- William Gilbert, physician to Elizabeth I, carves a lodestone into a sphere he calls a terrella, 'little Earth', walks a tiny compass across its surface, and the needle does exactly what ships' compasses do at sea. T2: the claim that came out of it -- the needle is not being pulled by the Pole Star or by a magnetic island at the north; the EARTH ITSELF is a giant magnet. He argued it by MODEL, which is why De Magnete is often called the first modern book of experimental science. T2b: the dip -- compass-maker Robert Norman had noticed in 1581 that a balanced needle tilts downward in England; Gilbert reproduced that tilt on his sphere and showed the angle grows toward the poles, a model predicting a real shipboard measurement. T3: Gilbert also SPLIT what everyone had lumped together -- rubbed amber attracts scraps of anything and then stops; lodestone pulls iron only, permanently, and points. He coined the word electricus, from the Greek for amber, for the first kind, and it took Oersted's needle 220 years to join the two back together. T3b: the second terrella, three centuries later -- Kristian Birkeland put a magnetised sphere coated in phosphorescent paint inside a vacuum chamber, fired electrons at it, and glowing rings appeared around its poles; he argued the aurora is charged particles from the SUN funnelled down Earth's field lines. T4: he was ridiculed for decades because the authorities of the day held that currents could not cross the vacuum of space; Birkeland died in 1917 without an answer, and in 1967 a satellite flying through the auroral zone found the field-aligned currents that now carry his name. T4b: what the field does for you -- the same magnetosphere that paints the aurora deflects most of the solar wind; satellites and astronauts outside it take the hit directly. T5: MYSTERY RUNG -- the field is generated by liquid iron circulating in the outer core, a self-sustaining dynamo, and the rocks record that it has REVERSED north and south many times, most recently about 780,000 years ago. Why it flips, and when the next flip comes, nobody can predict. T5b: kid invitation -- the aurora is the one item here you can walk outside and check; and the magnetic pole has moved measurably within living memory, drifting fast toward Siberia.
source: Grokipedia: /page/Terrella, /page/De_Magnete, /page/William_Gilbert_(physicist), /page/Earth's_magnetic_field, /page/Magnet, /page/Paleomagnetism; University of Oslo research news 'The king of northern lights' and Wikipedia: Birkeland_current (vacuum-chamber terrella with phosphorescent coating; ridicule because space was held to be a currentless vacuum; 1967 satellite confirmation of field-aligned currents)
framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder -- the spine is the METHOD (build a scale model and test the planet against it), displayed on two named cases 300 years apart, closing on an open question. Payoff: T3b/T4 -- Birkeland's glowing sphere and his fifty-year vindication. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: Gilbert got the right conclusion from the wrong mechanism -- he thought Earth's iron body was permanently magnetised; the modern answer is a liquid-core dynamo, and the ladder must say so rather than making Gilbert prematurely right. Second rail: the dynamo as the SOURCE is settled; the reversal mechanism and timing are NOT -- say 'nobody can predict' and never let a distractor on that rung secretly be the truth. Distractor mine is unusually rich: the genuine pre-Gilbert explanations -- a magnetic mountain or island at the pole, the Pole Star pulling the needle, and the widely believed claim that garlic destroys a compass's power, which Gilbert actually tested and refuted; for Birkeland, the rival views that auroras were sunlight reflected from polar ice or self-luminous high air with no solar cause. LANE, IMPORTANT: keep the reversal rung on the DYNAMO MYSTERY, never on seafloor magnetic stripes -- those are the Wegener/plate-tectonics evidence and belong to the earth-science Wegener ladder and to geography's map-moves ladder.
history_overlap: geography bank: aurora viewing places / northern-lights tour and magnetic-north navigation, plus its 'how we know the map moves' Wegener ladder which owns the seafloor magnetic stripes -- science here must key Gilbert's terrella test, Birkeland's ridicule and 1967 vindication, and the reversal mystery only.

name: The same machine run backwards: motor and generator
scope: THEME ladder -- one law read in two directions, displayed on named machines. T1: Faraday's copper disc spun between magnet poles in 1831 gave a steady current from muscle power alone, the first generator; feed current into the same disc and it spins itself. T2: the accident that proved it at industrial scale -- at the Vienna exposition of 1873, Zenobe Gramme's partner Hippolyte Fontaine carelessly wired one dynamo's output into a second dynamo, and the second machine's shaft started turning. A generator running backwards is a motor, and nobody had meant to demonstrate it. T3: the mechanism both ways -- a current sitting in a magnetic field feels a sideways push (motor); a wire pushed sideways through a magnetic field has current pushed along it (generator). One piece of physics, read in either direction. T3b: Lenz's rule as honest bookkeeping -- the induced current always opposes the change that produced it, so a generator gets HARDER to turn the more current you draw; you feel the electricity you are making in your legs on a bicycle dynamo, and energy is not free. T4: where you already own one -- the coil and magnet driving a loudspeaker cone, the motor spinning a hard drive, regenerative braking turning an electric car's motor into a generator to refill the battery, and an induction hob inducing eddy currents inside the PAN, which is why the pan gets hot and the glass beneath it does not. T4b: THE TEST -- drop a small strong magnet down a copper or aluminium pipe. Copper is not magnetic, yet the magnet sinks in slow motion, because its own motion induces circulating currents in the pipe whose fields push back. Lenz's rule made visible in three seconds. T5: the transformer is the third face of the same law -- Faraday's iron ring again -- and it works ONLY on alternating current, because no change means no induction; that is why you cannot transform DC and why the grid became AC. T5b: honest caveat -- a perfectly reversible machine is a schoolbook idealisation; real motors and generators are wound, geared and cooled for one job, so 'run it backwards' is true in principle and engineered around in practice.
source: Grokipedia: /page/Electromagnetic_induction, /page/Dynamo, /page/Faraday's_law_of_induction, /page/Induction_motor, /page/Alternator; Wikipedia: Gramme_machine (Fontaine's accidental cross-connection at the 1873 Vienna exposition; Pacinotti's earlier machine as inspiration), Faraday's_law_of_induction (only a CHANGING field induces current)
framing_note: CONCEPT/THEME ladder -- the analytic backbone rung of this sub-strand and the one that ties the historical ladders to machines the kid already owns. Payoff: T4b, the magnet falling in slow motion down a copper pipe -- a genuine test-it-yourself gem that costs almost nothing and looks impossible. Second payoff: T2, the 1873 accident. HARD ACCURACY RAIL: state Lenz's rule as CONSERVATION OF ENERGY, never as nature 'resisting' or 'wanting' -- anthropomorphising is banned; and do not overclaim strict reversibility of real machines (T5b exists to prevent that). Distractor mine = the live wrong ideas of the era -- perpetual-motion schemes built on exactly this misunderstanding (a respectable-sounding error, which is the point), the Gramme-versus-Pacinotti priority question, and the persistent wrong expectation that a magnet held still near a coil should give a steady current. Anti-restatement: on the copper-pipe rung the stem must NOT mention induced currents before asking why the magnet falls slowly. LANE: induction-hob COOKING technique belongs to the cooking bank; science owns only the eddy-current mechanism.
